title: Godzilla Minus One- A beautiful film with a meh ending

commenti.body: [removed]

>It reinforces the original intention of Godzilla that seems to have been forgotten, which is to serve as a metaphor/symbol and catalyst as a result for the brutality of war.

I think the intention of Godzilla Minus One was to show off some sweet VFX and so I wasn't surprised at all when I saw the director credited with the VFX, as well. All of the non-Godzilla scenes are cheesy, on the nose, and mostly poorly acted (I thought the lead was especially awful).

I ended up enjoying the movie because the Godzilla stuff was fun, but I don't think Yamazaki cared about any allegories. It almost felt opposite of the message about the brutality/effects of war because the human element seemed to exist just as a basis for Godzilla destroying everything.

What I do agree with, though, is how awful the ending was. Not only does he live, but so does she, and with perfect Neutrogena-commercial level skin, no less.

Yes, finally! Your comment is spot on. Especially about what Godzilla truly represents. 

I loved the Godzilla scenes, especially when it was chasing the boat. Outside of the Godzilla scenes, I felt the acting was overly dramatic for me. Maybe I am an asshole, idk.

I actually put the overdramatic acting aside when I thought the girl had died. Though I had very little emotional attachment to any of the characters, I found it a nice touch to kill off one of the main characters in the middle of the plot. However, only for her to have survived an explosion of that magnitude baffled me and ultimately took my rating from a 4 to a 3, and all the sads.

I was just thinking how this movie literally just needed to end at the docks with the main character hugging Akiko and acknowledging that he is her father. Cue credits, perfect ending. I'd be fascinated to know why the director chose to pull the punch and made it so cheesy at the end.
I feel like they decided to give it a more “kaiju-feel” ending, which is why they made it so cheesy? Might sound dumb and doesn’t justify that ending imo, but I think that’s why
I think you're right but it feels like such a weird thing to throw at the end for an otherwise fairly grounded movie.

The one thing people don't talk about enough, but has always been critical in a Godzilla movie; Godzilla is never defeated by brute power. Science is always what beats him.

Original Godzilla film: They beat him with that underwater/oxygen machine.

Godzilla 1985: They beat him by tricking him to walk into a volcano.

Shin Godzilla: They incapacitate him/freeze him from the inside out.

Godzilla Minus One: They use the water pressure trick to break him.

Hell, even in Godzilla vs Kong, he beats Kong, but loses to the robotic version of himself.

The theme is always the same; you can't beat him with flat out warfare/military power. Science is what defeats Godzilla.

I'm sorry, but I don't agree with you at all. The acting wasn't amazing but it wasn't bad either. The character parts were my favorite parts of the film. 

\> It almost felt opposite of the message about the brutality/effects of war because the human element seemed to exist just as a basis for Godzilla destroying everything.

What do you even mean by this? How are you supposed to show the brutality of people being killed without showing their humanity? Moreover, all the main characters survived in the end, so your comment makes even less sense in this context. 

Also, although I thought Noriko surviving at the end wasn't necessary, I still enjoyed it and almost cried. Besides, Godzilla killing everyone wasn't the point of the movie. The character part of the movie centered around Kamiki's guilt and the disregard of Japan for lives in the war. By making the final decision to live, it dispels the narrative of honorable sacrifice and shows the value of human life over war.
It’d be way more powerful if the father died rather than getting a Hollywood ending. Disappointing.

I agree wholeheartedly. I feel like such a tragic and devastating story with its immense amount of historical trauma deserved some semblance of a hopeful ending—or at the very least a content one. I can’t really understand the criticism of it being “cheesy” since it obviously seemed to indicate a parallel with Godzilla’s revival.

The ending was objectively horrible.

If that ending was an option, don’t have her be blown away but 100mph winds filled with rubble and other objects that would each likely kill her upon impact.

I should watch this film. I've always been taken by the film critic quote re: Godzilla...."The metaphor that ate Tokyo"; with the allusion to Hiroshima/Nagasaki as visible as a nuclear fireball.

The title intrigues me ...if it were "T-minus One" it would be clearer still. The second hand of the clock is just prior to midnight.

For me, the ending is earned. After everything Koichi (and by proxy, the audience) experiences, that jolt of happiness is cathartic. That said, the "bruise" on Noriko's neck means that their ending isn't as happy as you would initially think.
